body:
**`navigation` → resolved by #2994** (merged). Not promoted, and not deleted.

The additions-only list above says "Promote `navigation` into `ActionType`". That was the wrong call, for a reason worth recording because it applies to the two rows below it as well:

**The spec does not lack the concept — it spells it differently.** `type: 'url'` *is* "go to a location", with `openIn: 'self' | 'new-tab'` for the tab choice. Promoting `navigation` would have put a second spec name on one operation, which is the failure this whole track is named after, committed one level up.

Deleting was worse, because it is silent: `{ type: 'navigation', to: … }` is authored today (`element:button` CTAs), and without the case the action falls through to `executeActionSchema`, which returns `{ success: true }` — a green toast that navigates nowhere. That is #2960's trap, reached via a cleanup.

And the alias had **already drifted**, which is the ordinary outcome of two implementations of one concept. `executeNavigation` was quietly the weaker of the two: no `${param.X}` interpolation, `openIn` ignored, no `apiBase` promotion, no `/api/…` full-page short-circuit. So `{ type: 'navigation', to: '/x?p=${param.p}' }` shipped the literal `${param.p}` while the identical `url` action resolved it.

Resolved as a **declared alias** — `ObjectUiLocalActionType`, the treatment #2985 gave the page-visualization names — with both names routed through one navigator. So: **a dialect row has a third option next to promote and delete, and it is often the right one.**

The guard is structural rather than another assertion: built-in dispatch is now a table typed `Record<RunnableActionType, …>`, so an `ActionType` the spec **adds** stops compiling until an executor exists — #2942's "validates at save, renders nothing at run time" class, made a build error for actions.

---

## Next item, pre-checked: `combo` is the same shape

The list says "Promote or delete `combo` (`plugin-charts/normalizeChartSchema.ts:63`)". It is a third case of the above, and the spec settles it outright:

```ts
// spec/src/ui/chart.zod.ts — ChartSeriesSchema
/** Series type override (combo charts) */
type: ChartTypeSchema.optional().describe('Override chart type for this series'),
```

The spec already models combo charts, **per-series**, and says so in the field's own doc comment. `combo` as a top-level `chartType` is a redundant container name for "the series have mixed families" — structurally identical to the argument the spec's own taxonomy note already makes about stacking:

> stacking is not a chart family, it is a property of the series (`ChartSeries.stack`) … One `bar` family plus a series-level stack group expresses all three without multiplying the taxonomy.

So `combo` is not a capability the spec lacks. Unlike `navigation`, though, this one is a real behavior change in `plugin-charts` — `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx:819` branches on `chartType === 'combo'`, and the honest version derives "is combo" from whether `series[].type` varies. Wants its own PR.

The other two rows are unchanged and both need the framework: `ActionType` (6) vs `WidgetActionTypeSchema` (5) differ only by `form`, and deriving `ListChartConfigSchema.chartType` via `.extract([...])` is spec-side.

## Progress — three PRs, and one correction to Track C's premise

### Track A — done, framework [#4061](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/4061)

All three orphans deleted, zero-consumer re-verified by grep across framework `packages/` + `apps/`, objectui, and cloud on the current merge base.

Two things the issue's table did not anticipate:

**`AggregationFunctionEnum` also collided by name.** It exported a *type* called `AggregationFunction`; `data/query.zod.ts` exports a *value* of that name. Same identifier, two declaration spaces, different members (`percentile/median/stddev/variance` vs `array_agg/string_agg`).

**The `filters` key could not simply go with `FilterOperator`.** `check:docs` rejects deleting an authorable object key without a tombstone + a D2 conversion + a `major` FROM→TO mapping (ADR-0104) — the right rule, and the wrong trade for a shape nothing validated and no author writes, since Track A is meant to carry no migration. The key stays, retyped `z.unknown()` with the same NOT-YET-ENFORCED marker as `SubscriptionEventSchema.filters` (`api/realtime.zod.ts`). The two subscription surfaces now describe event filtering identically, and neither implies enforcement that does not exist.

Four generated ratchets had to move with the deletions — `json-schema.manifest.json`, `authorable-surface.json`, `api-surface.json`, and both the reference docs and the `objectstack-ui` skill reference index.

### Additions-only — done, framework [#4070](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/4070)

Three of the four items, plus a fork the audit did not name:

- **`ChartTypeSchema` admits `combo`.** The taxonomy could not name the family the rest of `chart.zod.ts` is written for: `ChartSeriesSchema.type` says *"combo charts"* in its own doc comment, and `ChartSeriesSchema.yAxis` binds left/right, which is only meaningful for mixed marks.
- **`WidgetActionTypeSchema` is `ActionType`.** Confirmed the issue's reading in objectui's code: `DashboardRenderer` routes everything except a raw `url` into the `ActionRunner`, deliberately, per the comment recording objectstack#3528.
- **`ListChartConfigSchema.chartType` is `ChartTypeSchema.extract([...])`** — same five members. `.extract` does resolve through the `lazySchema` proxy.
- **`@objectstack/lint`'s chart-family set derives from the taxonomy.** Not in the audit, and worth naming: `validate-widget-bindings`' hand-written list decides which widgets need a `chartConfig` measure mapping, and an unlisted family reads as *"not a chart"* — so the widget **passes** validation instead of being reported. `combo` was exactly that case; pinning the old list back reproduces it (zero findings).

`app-showcase`'s coverage test — a ratchet already in place — failed the moment `combo` was admitted, and the Chart Gallery now demonstrates it.

**`navigation` was deliberately not promoted**, against the issue's suggestion. `ActionRunner.executeNavigation` is a strictly weaker `executeUrl` (no `${param.X}` interpolation, no `apiBase` promotion, no `openIn`) differing only by a `replace` option, and its one live producer is the SDUI `element:button` `action` prop — which `ElementButtonPropsSchema` **does not model at all**. Promoting the name would put a second spelling of *navigate* into a closed vocabulary (members can't be removed later, per this issue's own rule) without closing the gap that actually exists. Filing the `element:button.action` gap separately.

### objectui — merged, #2989

The **third** operator translation table, which the audit's Track B did not cover: `view-config-utils`' `SPEC_TO_BUILDER_OP` resolved **10 of the 19** canonical `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS`. Executed against the real spec:

```
OLD table could not resolve 9 of 19 canonical view operators:
  not_equals, starts_with, ends_with, greater_than, less_than,
  greater_than_or_equal, less_than_or_equal, is_null, is_not_null
```

Same cause as #2974 — spellings enumerated by hand — so it is now derived from the spec's canonical list plus `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES`, folded case- and separator-insensitively. `@object-ui/components` exports `FILTER_BUILDER_OPERATORS` so the mapping asserts against the builder's real vocabulary. To be precise about severity: `toFilterGroup` has no in-repo caller, so this was a public-API defect, not a live bug.

### Correction: Track C's stated trigger is gone

The issue records that `BUILDER_TO_SPEC_OP` / `toSpecFilter` (`view-config-utils.ts:46`) emit `'not in'`, `before` and `after` verbatim, and objectstack#3948 cites that file as its reachable trigger. **Both had zero callers anywhere in the repo** — not exported from `@object-ui/plugin-view`, not even referenced by a test; they were left behind when the studio's spec-driven inspector replaced `buildViewConfigSchema`. They are deleted in #2989.

With #2974 merged and this deleted, **objectui no longer has a live path emitting those spellings.** Framework `main` has also since added `before`/`after` to `AST_OPERATOR_MAP`, which removes the trigger from the other side. objectstack#3948's remaining exposure is the server-side silent-drop itself — which is still real, and still what blocks Track C's `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` narrowing. The reachability argument in that issue needs updating, not the fix.

### Still blocked, unchanged

Track C prerequisites 1–4 stand as written. Nothing in these three PRs narrows a vocabulary, so none of them touches stored metadata.

## All three PRs merged

| | Repo | PR |
|---|---|---|
| **Track A** — orphans deleted | framework | objectstack-ai/objectstack#4061 ✅ |
| **Additions-only** — vocabularies admit what renders | framework | objectstack-ai/objectstack#4070 ✅ |
| Third operator table pinned to the spec | objectui | #2989 ✅ |

### Six generated ratchets had to move with the changes

Worth recording, because the audit did not anticipate any of them and each one refused the change until it was satisfied:

| Gate | What it caught |
|---|---|
| `check:docs` (manifest) | five unpublished schemas — would silently delete their reference pages |
| `check:docs` (key removal) | `EventSubscription.filters` needs a tombstone + D2 conversion (ADR-0104) |
| `check:authorable-surface` | the seven keys of the two deleted objects |
| `check:api-surface` | the eight removed exports |
| `check:skill-refs` / `check:react-blocks` | the skill reference index and the react-blocks contract inline the enums |
| `app-showcase` coverage + `check-i18n-coverage` | admitting `combo` demands a gallery widget — and that widget's title demands a zh-CN translation |

The last one is the useful lesson for whoever picks up Track C: adding a member to a `ui/` vocabulary is not a one-line change. It is one line plus five generated artefacts and a showcase demonstration. All twelve of `packages/spec`'s `check:*` scripts pass locally on both merged branches — running them before pushing is much cheaper than discovering them one CI round at a time.

### Track C — still blocked, and one premise now retired

Prerequisites 1–4 stand. But the *trigger* the issue and objectstack-ai/objectstack#3948 both cite — `BUILDER_TO_SPEC_OP` / `toSpecFilter` at `view-config-utils.ts:46` emitting `'not in'`, `before`, `after` — was **already dead code**, with no caller anywhere in objectui and no public export. It is deleted in #2989.

So objectui no longer has a live path emitting those spellings, and framework `main` has separately added `before`/`after` to `AST_OPERATOR_MAP`. **objectstack#3948's silent-drop is still real and still blocks narrowing `VALID_AST_OPERATORS`** — a driver that skips an unknown operator instead of throwing makes any narrowing untestable. What no longer holds is its reachability argument.

Follow-up filed: #2997 — SDUI `element:button` executes an `action` prop the spec does not declare, which is where the `navigation` action type actually lives.

**`combo` → resolved by #3004** (merged). Derived from the series, not promoted and not deleted.

Same shape as `navigation` (#2994), and the check was one grep. The additions-only list said "Promote or delete `combo`". The spec **already models a combo chart**, per-series, and its own field comment says so:

```ts
// spec/src/ui/chart.zod.ts — ChartSeriesSchema
/** Series type override (combo charts) */
type: ChartTypeSchema.optional().describe('Override chart type for this series'),
```

Exactly the reasoning the spec's own taxonomy note applies to stacking — `ChartSeries.stack` rather than a `stacked-bar` family. So `combo` is not a name an author should reach for; `effectiveChartFamily` derives it, and `combo` stays a documented renderer-local marker (internal callers pass it today).

## The row was the least interesting thing wrong at that line

Three silent bugs, all on the path a spec author takes, none visible from an enum-coverage angle:

1. **The per-series override was parsed, carried, and then dropped.** Only the `chartType === 'combo'` branch read `series[].chartType`, so `{ type: 'bar', series: [{ name: 'revenue' }, { name: 'margin', type: 'line' }] }` drew `margin` as a bar. An existing unit test even asserted the value was carried — it just never got drawn.
2. **A spec-shape `series` rendered nothing at all.** `series` is the one binding both shapes spell with the *same key*, so `ChartRenderer`'s blanket "internal props win" rule let the author's `[{ name }]` shadow the normalized `[{ dataKey }]` and reach a renderer that reads `dataKey`. Every other spec binding has a distinct name (`xAxis` vs `xAxisKey`), which is why only this one broke — and why the isolated normalization tests all passed over a dead path. Found by probing the real path rather than trusting those tests. Fixed here rather than filed, because (1) alone would have been a fix no spec author could reach.
3. **The combo branch's `area` arm was unreachable.** Its container was `BarChart`, and Recharts renders an `<Area>` child of `BarChart` as nothing — so an authored combo with an `area` series drew a blank series. Container is now `ComposedChart`.

`ChartRendererProps.series` also now accepts both shapes; it was typed internal-only, so writing the protocol correctly was a **type error on code that works** — the same trap `ActionType`-missing-`form` was in #2985.

---

## Where this track stands

Three "renderer-local dialect" rows are now settled, and all three came out the same way: **the spec already had the name, spelled differently.** `navigation`→`url`, `combo`→`ChartSeries.type`, and #2985's page-visualization names. The promote/delete framing missed the right option every time. Recorded as Correction 4 in the audit doc.

Remaining items on this list both need the framework, and are worth **one spec PR** — additions-only, no migration:

- `ActionType` (6) vs `WidgetActionTypeSchema` (5) differ only by `form`, and dashboard header actions funnel into the same `ActionRunner` that implements it, so the narrower enum rejects at validation what the shared dispatcher executes.
- Derive `ListChartConfigSchema.chartType` (5) from `ChartTypeSchema` (19) via `.extract([...])` instead of retyping it.

Incidentally, #3008 added the `@objectstack/spec` devDep to `plugin-charts`, so the audit's "packages lacking the devDep" count is converging on its own.

Track C is still blocked on objectstack-ai/objectstack#3948 item 1 — unchanged.

## Track C 的两个前置条件已完成 — 现在只剩生产数据扫描

自上次更新后又合了一个 PR，并核对了阻塞项的真实状态。**Track C 的技术前置条件已全部就绪。**

### 前置条件 1 — 驱动抛错而非静默丢弃：**早已完成**

不是本次做的 —— 核对 framework `main` 时发现它已经在了。`driver-sql` 的 `applyFilters`（`sql-driver.ts:4743`）和 `driver-memory`（`memory-driver.ts:811`/`:819`）都会对未识别的操作符抛错，注释里带 `#3948`，并各有专门的回归测试。`VALID_AST_OPERATORS` 现在也从 `AST_OPERATOR_MAP` 的 key 派生，"一个表里有、另一个表里没有"这种失配已被结构性关掉。

**所以收窄 `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` 现在是可测的** —— 这正是本 issue 当初说必须先有的东西。objectstack#3948 仍然 open，但它的标题缺陷已修；我已在那边留下逐项核对（item 1 ✅、item 3 ✅、item 2 ❌ 且只剩报错质量问题），并建议关闭或改标题，否则本 issue 会一直看起来阻塞在已交付的东西上。

### 前置条件 2 — `saveMeta` 持久化归一化后的 filter：**objectstack-ai/objectstack#4107 已合并** ✅

`ViewFilterRuleSchema.operator` 是 `z.preprocess(normalizeFilterOperator, …)`，校验时已经把 `notEquals`/`gt`/`isNull` 折叠成规范拼写 —— 然后结果被丢掉，因为 `saveMetaItem` 按原样持久化（这是有意的：`parsed.data` 会剥掉随 overlay 一起走的 Studio 辅助字段 `isPinned`/`isDefault`/`sortOrder`）。

结果不是"旧拼写活了下来"，而是**每次保存都在生成新的别名行**。所以别名表永远退不掉：重写全部现存行的迁移，在下一次 console 个性化 `PUT` 落地的那一刻就过期了。

`graftNormalizedOperators` 按**结构**并行遍历「作者原文」与 `parsed.data`，只搬一样东西:解析后与原文不同的 `operator`。没有路径清单 —— `ViewFilterRule[]` 目前有五处声明点，结构遍历全覆盖,以后新增的也覆盖;在这里手写路径表反而会复刻本 issue 要消灭的重复。两侧都必须是 string 才改,所以 `$`-token 的 `FilterCondition`（另一套操作符词汇）不会被误改;不增删、不重排、不填默认值 —— 一元 `{field, operator}` 形式不会因此长出 `value`,尽管 schema 自己的输出会。

行为变化要说清楚:`PUT` 之后 `GET` 返回的是规范拼写,不是作者写的那个。这是 spec 定义的拼写,而且 #2974 / #2989 已把 objectui 三张翻译表全部双向对齐到完整词汇表,所以每个渲染路径都认。**现存行未被触碰 —— 这只是止血,不是迁移。**

### 前置条件 4 — 派生而非重复:**已由架构约束解决,措辞需更新**

本 issue 写的是"`AST_OPERATOR_MAP` 和 `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES` 应来自同一张表,且 `filter.zod.ts:362` 不应把跨仓库手工同步写成机制"。现状:

- `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` **已经**从 `AST_OPERATOR_MAP` 派生;
- 两张表之间无法直接派生,原因是**分层方向**:`ui/` 导入 `data/`,所以 `data/filter.zod.ts` 不能反向导入 `ui/view.zod.ts` 的词汇表。这不是疏忽,注释里写明了;
- 替代机制是 `filter-view-operator-parity.test.ts`,断言 `AST_OPERATOR_MAP` 覆盖每个 `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` 成员和每个别名 key。

所以那句"跨仓库手工同步"已经不准确 —— 它现在是**仓内有断言的 parity**。真正彻底的做法是把视图操作符词汇表下移到 `shared/`,让两边都派生;但 parity 测试已经挡住漂移,收益是"一张表"而非"两张表 + 一个测试",价值中等。

### 只剩前置条件 3,而它不是 CI 能做的事

> 写任何迁移之前先扫生产。`sys_saved_report.query_json` 在读和写两侧都未校验,所以其内容无法静态枚举。

这需要访问真实部署的数据,我做不了。**这是 Track C 现在唯一的实质阻塞项**,而且它是运维动作而非代码改动。

### 下一步建议(按价值排序)

1. **扫生产**,统计 `sys_metadata` / `sys_sharing_rule.criteria_json` / `sys_saved_report.query_json` 里实际出现的操作符拼写分布。有了这个才能判断退别名表要写多大的迁移 —— 也可能发现绝大多数别名从未被真实使用,迁移范围远小于预期。
2. **处置 objectstack#3948**:关闭或改标题,并把 item 2(protocol 层拒绝 vs 透传)拆成独立的报错质量 issue。给未来的人看的账要对得上。
3. **objectstack-ai/objectui#2997**:SDUI `element:button.action` 未在 spec 声明 —— `navigation` 这个动作类型真正的落点,需要一次设计决策(三个选项已在 issue 里列出)。
4. **可选**:把视图操作符词汇表下移到 `shared/`,彻底闭合前置条件 4。

Status check while picking up what remained here — **Track A and the additions-only list are both already done**, so the framing above is stale. Recording it so nobody redoes the work.

## Track A — done (framework#4061)

All three orphan vocabularies retired, each with a tombstone comment explaining why it went rather than got reconciled:

| Vocabulary | Was at | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| `AggregationFunctionEnum` | `shared/enums.zod.ts` | gone; no residue in framework spec src |
| `FilterOperator` + `EventFilterCondition`/`EventFilterSchema` | `api/websocket.zod.ts` | gone |
| `ODataFilterOperatorSchema` | `api/odata.zod.ts` | gone |

I re-grepped for all three symbols across framework (`packages`/`apps`/`examples`) and objectui (`packages`/`apps`): zero consumers, comment-only hits. The `$filter`-is-an-opaque-string reasoning in the odata tombstone is worth keeping — an enum mixing operators with parentheses describes tokens, not a grammar, so a real OData implementation needs a parser that lowers onto `AST_OPERATOR_MAP` like every other entry point.

## Additions-only list — done (framework#4070)

- `combo` promoted into `ChartTypeSchema` — the taxonomy could not name the one family the rest of `chart.zod.ts` is written for (`ChartSeriesSchema.type` exists to override a series' type, `.yAxis` binds left/right, both of which only mean something for mixed marks).
- `WidgetActionTypeSchema` **is** `ActionType` now — and the disagreement was backwards from how this issue framed it: the narrower enum rejected at validation what the shared `ActionRunner` executes.
- `ListChartConfigSchema.chartType` derives via `ChartTypeSchema.extract([...])`.
- Bonus, and the sharpest of the four: `@objectstack/lint`'s chart-family set now derives from the taxonomy. Its omissions failed in the worst direction — an unlisted family read as "not a chart", so a widget with no measure mapping *passed* the binding validator.

## Track C prerequisite #2 — done (framework#4107)

`saveMeta` persists the normalized operator spellings, so the alias table can eventually be retired without new alias rows being created. Prerequisite #1 (objectstack#3948 item 1 — driver throws instead of skipping) is still open, so **Track C still should not start**.

## One objectui-side loose end, fixed

`combo` is promoted in framework main but not in a published spec version, so objectui still resolves the enum without it. My Tier-3 parity guard (#3011) asserted `dialect === ['combo']` exactly, which would have turned the eventual spec bump into a cryptic red test for whoever did the bump. Made it directional in objectui#3016 — the tracked set is now an upper bound, so adoption is green and only new dialect fails.

## Suggested edit to this issue

Track A and the additions-only section could be struck through, leaving Track C (blocked) plus prerequisite #1 as the only open work. Happy to do that if you'd rather it live in the issue body than a comment.

## Status sweep — this issue is now materially out of date, and that is costly

I picked up the two remaining additions-only items and found **both already shipped**, along with Track A and three of Track C's four prerequisites. I got as far as a framework worktree before checking. Recording the evidence so the next agent doesn't repeat that.

### Additions-only list — all four done

| Item | Landed |
|---|---|
| Promote `navigation` into `ActionType` | objectstack-ai/objectui#2994 — **not promoted**; resolved as a declared alias of `url` (see the comment above) |
| Promote or delete `combo` | objectstack-ai/objectui#3004 — **neither**; derived from `ChartSeries.type` |
| Reconcile `ActionType` (6) vs `WidgetActionTypeSchema` (5) | objectstack-ai/objectstack#4070 |
| Derive `ListChartConfigSchema.chartType` via `.extract()` | objectstack-ai/objectstack#4070 |

`WidgetActionTypeSchema` is now `lazySchema(() => ActionType.describe(…))` — the enum itself, not a subset — and `spec/src/ui/vocabulary-derivation.test.ts` pins both derivations (7/7 green on framework `main`).

### Track A — done

objectstack-ai/objectstack#4061 retired all three orphan operator vocabularies.

### Track C — the blocker is gone

The issue says *"Do not start before that lands."* It landed.

| Prerequisite | State |
|---|---|
| 1. Driver throws instead of skipping | **Done** — objectstack#4029 closed objectstack#3948. Verified in the source: `driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` now throws `Unrecognized filter operator "…" in a comparison triple`, and `driver-memory` matches. |
| 2. `saveMeta` persists the normalized `filter` subtree | **Done** — objectstack#4107. `graftNormalizedOperators` grafts the normalization back onto the verbatim body, so **saves no longer mint new legacy-alias rows.** That was the reason a migration could never converge. |
| 3. Scan production before writing any migration | **Open**, and not answerable from a checkout — `sys_saved_report.query_json` is unvalidated on both read and write, so its contents still cannot be enumerated statically. |
| 4. Derive, don't duplicate | **Done** — `VALID_AST_OPERATORS = new Set(Object.keys(AST_OPERATOR_MAP))`, and `data/filter.zod.ts` no longer documents a cross-repo hand-sync as the mechanism: it names `filter-view-operator-parity.test.ts` and explains why import-derivation is impossible (`ui/` imports `data/`, so `data/` cannot import back). |

**The risk profile in the Track C table has changed, which is the part worth re-reading before anyone acts on it.** Its two "do not" verdicts were both conditioned on silence:

- *"`VALID_AST_OPERATORS` — do not narrow. Removing a spelling converts a working bare-triple filter into a full-table scan with no error anywhere."* No longer true: the driver throws. Narrowing is now **loud**, so the verdict changes from prohibited to *needs a migration and a release note* — a different and much more tractable problem.
- *"`VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` aliases — needs migration. All ~30 aliases are actively being written to `sys_metadata` today."* No longer being written. What remains is repairing rows already stored, which is a one-shot job with an end, not a moving target.

So the honest remaining gate on Track C is prerequisite 3 alone — **survey what is actually stored** — and that is an ops task, not a code change. Nobody should narrow anything until someone has looked.

### Suggested bookkeeping

The issue body still reads "only one of them is safe to start today" and marks Track C blocked. It is the coordination surface for several agents working this in parallel, and stale text here costs real duplicated work — I nearly rebuilt #4070. Worth an edit rather than only this comment.

## Track C 重新评估 —— 第 4 项已完成,前三项建议**不要**做

按建议继续时,我先核对了 Track C 四个目标各自还剩什么风险。结论和 issue 原文不同,记录在此。

### ✅ 第 4 项已完成 —— objectstack-ai/objectstack#4153

*"`AggregationFunction`:三处必须同步"* —— 这是 Track C **唯一不需要扫生产**的一项,因为它不收窄任何东西。而且它不只是整洁问题,是**静默错数**:

| 位置 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `AggregationFunction`(spec) | 8 个成员 |
| `UNSUPPORTED_AGGREGATES`(dataset-compiler) | 2 个编译期拒绝 |
| `native-sql-strategy` 的 switch | 6 个 case + `default: COUNT(*)` |

8 − 2 = 6 = 六个 case,**今天**成立。给 spec 加第九个成员(`median`、`percentile`…),它会:通过编译器的门(不在 UNSUPPORTED 里)→ 被那个门的**报错文案**宣告为受支持(硬编码的散文列表,词汇表的第三份副本)→ 进 switch 匹配不到 → 落到 `default: COUNT(*)`。

**作者要中位数,拿到行数。没有报错,没有日志,dashboard 上是错的数字。** 和 #3948 同一个形状,只是换到分析 SQL 构建器。

改法是派生 + guard,零行为变化:switch 改成可断言覆盖的表,散文列表改成 `AggregationFunction.options` 减 `UNSUPPORTED_AGGREGATES`,新测试双向断言这个算术。**验证过有牙** —— 给 spec 加个假的 `median`,三条断言失败并点名它;同样的改动在此之前是绿的。

顺带发现但**没有一起修**、已单独立 objectstack-ai/objectstack#4157:同一个 `COUNT(*)` fallback 也会接住 `number`/`string`/`boolean` 类型的 metric —— 那是自定义 SQL **表达式**(`AggregationMetricType`),表达式被整个丢掉换成行数。dataset 产不出这种 metric,只有手写 Cube 能触发;改成返回 `col` 是分析 SQL 路径的行为变更,该有自己的测试矩阵。
